label: Section 338 Tariff on Canadian Goods
deltaNote: Talks collapsed late Aug 21; tariffs now cover ~$20B (C$28B) of Canadian goods — electronics, plastics, wood, paper, dairy, alcohol, cement, clothing, hockey equipment — about 5% of Canada's US-bound exports. Energy, potash, fish and critical minerals remain exempt.

label: Draft Deal: Steel/Aluminum & Auto Tariffs
contestNote: The reported draft terms (25% steel/aluminum, 15% autos) never became a signed agreement — talks broke down late Aug 21, hours before the deadline, with Carney citing 'uneconomic, unfair' last-minute US demands and Greer blaming Canada for walking back prior commitments. As of Sept 3, both sides still trade blame in public: Commerce Secretary Lutnick says Canada tanked talks for domestic political reasons, Carney says US negotiators shifted their own red lines since the collapse. No new talks scheduled.

label: Canada's Retaliatory Tariff Package
source: BNN Bloomberg / Dept. of Finance Canada
delta: took effect as scheduled, 12:01am ET Sept 8, 2026
deltaNote: Sliding 15/25/50% tariffs across ~893 tariff lines on C$27.6B of US goods went live on schedule; hours later the US countered with Sept 29 import bans on Canadian dairy, alcohol and motor vehicle products plus a threatened GSA procurement freeze. Carney signaled Sept 10 that Canada would hold off further retaliation for now, calling the Sept 8 US counter-measures 'relatively modest.'

label: Canada Worker & Business Support Package
deltaNote: EI eligibility changes (C$3.5B, waived 1-week wait + 20 extra weeks for long-tenured workers), Regional Tariff Response Initiative (C$1.5B), BDC liquidity (C$500M), Canada Strong Diversification Fund (C$2B).

label: Mexico Non-USMCA Baseline Tariff
contestNote: Sheinbaum says tariffs on Mexico 'did not change' from the pre-existing 10% non-USMCA rate; USTR gave the floated additional 10% concrete effect via a Section 301 forced-labor tariff implemented Jul 24, 2026 (USMCA-compliant goods remain exempt).

label: IEEPA Tariff Refund Liability
contestNote: Amount collected under the tariffs SCOTUS struck down Feb 20, 2026; refund mechanics still being litigated at the Court of International Trade, so the actual government payout remains undetermined.

label: US Net Tariff Revenue (Oct 2025–Jun 2026)
source: Richmond Fed / Penn Wharton Budget Model
deltaNote: Net of refunds tied to the IEEPA ruling

label: Canada GDP Impact by End-2026
source: Bank of Canada Monetary Policy Report, Jan 2026

label: US Household Tariff Cost, 2026
contestNote: Estimates range from $600-$900 (industry-aligned analyses) to $2,500 (Senate Joint Economic Committee Democrats); methodology and which tariffs are counted vary widely.

label: Canada Trade War Job-Loss Estimate
source: Peacock Tariff Consulting / Oxford Economics via Al Jazeera
contestNote: Trade consultant Ashley Kalyn's 100,000-job estimate has not been independently modeled by Statistics Canada; Oxford Economics' Tony Stillo separately estimates the tariff war shaves roughly 0.3 percentage points off Canadian GDP growth versus the pre-tariff path.

label: US Bans on Canadian Dairy, Alcohol & Motor Vehicle Imports
deltaNote: 5 Section 338 proclamations signed Sept 8 in response to Canada's same-day retaliation: bans cover most alcoholic beverages, whey/molasses dairy inputs, and motor vehicle products including motorcycles. A separate GSA directive threatens removing Canadian goods from over $50B in federal procurement schedules absent 'full and fair reciprocity.'

label: Bombardier US Sales Threat
contestNote: Trump says Bombardier products 'aren't good enough' and must build in the US; Bombardier says it already employs 3,500 US workers across 47 states, with wings built in Texas and flight-control systems in California, and spends $2.5B/yr with US suppliers.
